summary: Georgia's highest peak had a lookout by 1917 (per a 1973 recollection); the 1965 tower went to Southern Forest World; the present tower is open and rarely staffed.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict and the story reports both: first CCC tower 1935 (Georgia Highpoint) vs a lookout tower 1939 (Eastern US lookouts); present tower 1965 vs 1966 on the Georgia Highpoint page, with the 2023 newsletter giving 1965 for the circular tower we see today. The story no longer says the sources disagree on 1965: only Georgia Highpoint gives both dates. The newsletter caption dates the CCC stone tower to 1935 and its steel replacement to 1947; the story does not use the 1947 date. The 1965 move to Southern Forest World is on both the Eastern US lookouts and Georgia Highpoint pages; the tnlandforms row 'sfw museum ... brasstown-relocated' is a list entry, not a site visit. The Smith material is from a 1973 interview as quoted in the 2023 newsletter; the newsletter text is garbled in places, so each quote was taken from a single intact line. The brief's elevation (1443.2 m, from tnlandforms' 4735) differs from Georgia Highpoint's 4,784 ft summit figure; elevation is not a schema fact, so nothing was changed. The FIND Outdoors site-history page returned HTTP 503 twice and was not read. The brief's registration GFC US 906 was not verified. Current condition and access are from the Georgia Highpoint guide, not a site visit. No photos.
